persona.label: Rushed but qualified
persona.description: Busy professional between meetings. Terse, answers several things at once. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are between meetings and have about five minutes. Your first reply says something like "ok but make it fast, I'm busy." Use short, lowercase texts with no pleasantries. When asked something, answer it, and volunteer one or two related facts if it saves time. Round numbers the way people do ("about 520", "owe like 310k"). If the assistant is slow or repetitive, show mild impatience. You want a lower rate and you want to talk to someone today.

transcript.text: Hi Taylor, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
ok but make it fast, i'm busy. looking to lower my rate, currently at 7.25
Got it, I'll keep this quick. Roughly what's your home worth, and about how much do you still owe on the mortgage?

objections.rationale: The borrower said "make it fast, i'm busy" but had already agreed to answer by text. The agent acknowledged it ("Got it, I'll keep this quick"), batched questions, and finished in three turns. It never offered the playbook's callback-time option, though the borrower's "ok" made that less necessary.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are short and warm, and they adapt to a rushed borrower. The agent combined two questions per turn, gave the credit buckets inline, and added a brief reassurance ("This is just your own estimate. Nothing gets checked here."). It read like a sharp coordinator texting.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower asked "can someone call me today?" and at [6] got a direct "Yes" with specifics: a licensed loan officer will call "at this number, usually within 5 minutes," may confirm a few details, and will go over rate options. Expectations were set honestly and nothing was overpromised.
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete: $520k value, $310k balance, 7.25% current rate, primary residence, 740+ self-reported credit, ASAP timeline, and LTV 0.596, which is correct. It flags that the borrower is busy and wants a call today, and gives an actionable next step (call now, keep it brief). A loan officer could act on it immediately.

annotations.note: Clearly discloses "an automated assistant," ties the text to the borrower's inquiry, and gives the STOP opt-out up front.
"Got it, I'll keep this quick" acknowledges the time pressure, then asks home value and balance together to save a round trip.
Lists the credit range options and reassures that "Nothing gets checked here," which lowers friction without implying any credit decision.

Answers the call-today request directly, with the channel and timing ("call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes"), and frames the loan officer as the one who "will go over your rate options," with no rate hinted.
The agent never offered a scheduled callback time as an alternative to texting, which the busy playbook calls for, though the borrower's "ok" made this a minor gap.

judge.overall_notes: This was a clean, efficient qualification of a rushed borrower with no compliance issues and an honest, specific handoff. The only small gap is skipping the explicit callback-time option from the busy playbook.
